summary: First-principles design review, iteration 5 (full record in review_loop/scrutiny_05.md). This pass executed the audits verdict_04 explicitly deferred — eval_all_trajectories.py / collect_results.py, the H1 signature granularity, the 6e-4 recompute tolerance — and found that the EVALUATION DRIVER, the sole producer of every trajectory_eval artifact the metric layer consumes, would have corrupted the headline comparison in three independent ways. (1) It hardcoded its output to results/branching/, so evaluating the vanilla control would have OVERWRITTEN the treatment's eval files (R2.5), and the documented RESULTS SS5 workflow (--compare-eval results/resample_t0.7) was physically unproducible. (2) Its default dedup dropped duplicate AND empty patches from the eval record, redefining metric-time k as #unique-nonempty-patches instead of #trajectories-produced: vanilla's duplicate patches ARE the mode-collapse signal under study, and erasing them deflates vanilla's k, drags the matched k* down, subsamples the treatment's coverage via the Chen estimator while vanilla keeps plain any-pass, and compresses the H1 rarefaction comparison (worked example: 4xF+1xP gives true pass@1=0.2 but deduped pass@1=0.5). The most carefully pre-registered endpoint is worthless if the artifact feeding it measures a different denominator. (3) The best-of 'primary' row leaked as a null trajectory_id that load_eval counted but load_eval_by_tid dropped, so the coverage table's n could desync from every tid-joined analysis reading the same file. Fixed by a rewritten driver: --results-dir arm isolation, propagate_duplicate_results (one eval row per genuine trajectory; duplicates inherit their representative's outcome marked deduped_from — exact under the deterministic harness; empty patches resolved:false without a container run), primary normalization, keep-last per tid, greedy-keyed pass@1, lazy swebench import so the helpers are stage-testable. Second find: re-run staleness — phased_decisions.log is append-mode while predictions keep-last and metadata.json is overwritten, yet load_entropy and tau_sweep.parse_instance read the FIRST strategy-proposal block, joining a stale run's entropy/partition to the new run's trajectories; both now read the LAST block (tested), and the eval driver dedupes resample re-run appends. Third find: the confirmatory H1 endpoint conflates diversity with patch-PRODUCTION rate (an empty patch lowers rarefied distinct exactly like a duplicate), so an H1 rejection could be over-read as mode-collapse escape when vanilla merely aborted more; compare() now reports nonempty_patch_fraction per arm plus a descriptive non-empty-only rarefied-gain robustness row (k*_ne = min nonempty count), fixed pre-data with the endpoint UNCHANGED, and the exact-signature granularity's bias direction (conservative: it inflates the sampling-noisier CONTROL's distinct count) is now stated in print. Also: budget accounting's exclusion of proposer/intent/NLI calls (absent from .traj.json) is disclosed with its direction; the eval summary's 'pass@1 (greedy)' was actually the best-of row, now keyed to t0/run0. Two spec amendments applied under ratchet v2 (applied_05_eval_record_completeness.md, applied_05_h1_productivity_diagnostics.md): R4.1 eval-record completeness + loader consistency + last-block rule, R7.2 arm-isolated eval outputs, R4.2 productivity diagnostics + granularity disclosure, R6.3 disclosed accounting exclusions — all add obligations implemented and tested this same iteration; nothing flips to pass for the existing artifact and the confirmatory endpoint is untouched (the new diagnostics can only DOWNGRADE a treatment win). 77 tests pass (was 69; +8: 4 eval-driver, 3 compute_metrics, 1 tau_sweep), py_compile clean, compute_metrics/tau_sweep re-run end-to-end on real artifacts, driver --help smokes pass. The existing results/branching eval files were produced by the old driver and are documented as smoke-only; the pre-registered runs regenerate all eval records with the fixed driver (the campaign worktree's run_campaign.py already calls it with --results-dir and stays API-compatible). Because real evidence-pipeline flaws were found and fixed, gold_standard_met is FALSE per the charter; the loop should pass once more over the post-fix design.

issues_found.title: Eval driver hardcoded results/branching as its output dir: evaluating the control would overwrite the treatment's eval files, and the documented SS5 comparison workflow was physically unproducible
issues_found.rationale: There is no other producer of trajectory_eval_<iid>.json. Fixed with --results-dir end-to-end (output, predictions default, temp files, arm-scoped run_ids); RESULTS SS5 now documents the per-arm eval step; R7.2 amended to require arm isolation of eval outputs.

issues_found.title: Default eval dedup dropped duplicate AND empty patches from the eval record, redefining metric-time k as #unique-nonempty-patches — deleting the vanilla arm's mode-collapse duplicates (the phenomenon under study) and corrupting matched-k* for both H1 and H2
issues_found.rationale: The Chen estimator's (n,c) must count what the arm produced: 4xF+1xP is pass@1=0.2, not the deduped 0.5; vanilla's deflated k drags k* down and subsamples the treatment's coverage while vanilla keeps any-pass. Fixed via propagate_duplicate_results (duplicates inherit the representative's outcome, marked; empties are failed draws); R4.1 amended (eval-record completeness); 4 new stage tests.

issues_found.title: Re-run staleness: all post-hoc parsers (load_entropy, tau_sweep.parse_instance) read the FIRST strategy-proposal block of the append-mode decisions log, while predictions keep-last and metadata.json is overwritten — a re-run instance gets the old run's entropy/partition joined to the new run's trajectories
issues_found.rationale: Wrong strata, wrong gate reconstruction, wrong dominant trajectory on any re-run instance. Both parsers now read the LAST block (tested); the eval driver also keeps the last occurrence per tid for the resample file, which has no batch separators.

issues_found.title: H1 conflates diversity with patch-production rate: an empty patch lowers the rarefied distinct count exactly like a duplicate, so a confirmatory diversity win could be a completion-rate artifact over-read as mode-collapse escape
issues_found.rationale: Endpoint deliberately UNCHANGED (no forking paths); compare() now reports nonempty_patch_fraction per arm and a descriptive non-empty-only rarefied gain at k*_ne, fixed pre-data, with the reading rule in RESULTS SS3 — the diagnostic can only downgrade a treatment win. Granularity bias direction (conservative) also now stated in print. Rejected alternatives recorded in applied_05_h1_productivity_diagnostics.md.

issues_found.title: Metric loaders disagreed about null trajectory ids: load_eval counted them, load_eval_by_tid dropped them — the coverage table's n could desync from every tid-joined analysis reading the same eval file
issues_found.rationale: Both loaders now drop the best-of duplicate whether its id is 'primary' or null, and the eval driver normalizes at write time (tested at both layers).

issues_found.title: Budget accounting silently excluded the treatment arm's proposer/intent/NLI calls (absent from .traj.json transcripts); the eval summary's 'pass@1 (greedy)' was actually the best-of primary row
issues_found.rationale: Exclusion is bounded (1 proposer call + 10 NLI pair passes of a 0.4B model vs k full trajectories) and now direction-disclosed in budget_audit fairness_note + RESULTS SS5 + R6.3; pass@1 now keyed to t0/run0 so the saved artifact field is truthful.
